jurs: Churches of England and Ireland (royal supremacy)
In Ireland the established church is reformed but most parishes and people remain Roman.
Evangelical church orders (princes and city councils)
Synods and city councils in Switzerland, Geneva and East Frisia; Bucer and à Lasco are now in England.
Gallican Church (Roman communion, under the Primate of Lyon)
Rome still confirms French bishops under the 1516 Concordat; Lyon hears appeals and convenes the national synod.
Rhineland Gnesio-Catholics in union with Lyon
Gnesio-Catholic in confession, under the Lyon primacy by special arrangement; not merged into the Gallican Church.
Territorial churches bound by the agreed confession of Cranmer's council; the Churches of England and Ireland are shown separately.
Bishops consecrated by Swedish bishops in the old succession; Bohemia keeps its consistory after the 1575 union.
Hardline Reformed churches (Kirk, Geneva, Huguenot synods)
Churches that rejected the Cranmerian settlement: Scotland, Geneva and Vaud, Béarn and the Huguenot south.
Includes Orthodox Christians under Ottoman, Venetian and Lithuanian rule.
Self-governing archbishopric covering Macedonia, Albania and much of Serbia.
Moscow chose its own metropolitans after rejecting the Union of Florence; Constantinople had not recognised this.
Western-Rite Orthodox church (primate at Narva, in communion with Moscow)
Western liturgy and Gnesio-derived theology, Orthodox bishops and creed; the filioque and unleavened bread were given up as the price of the primacy.
The bishops accepted union with Rome; many parishes, the Lviv brotherhood and the Ostroh circle did not.
